metadata.title: AI Electrician Quoting Platform — Conversational Job Capture Data Model
metadata.regulatory_framework: BS 7671:2018+A2:2022 and BS 7671:2018+A4:2026 (mandatory from 15 Oct 2026), Part P Building Regulations, Approved Document S (EV chargers)

universal_questions.question: What type of property is this?
universal_questions.rationale: Determines access difficulty, cable routing and DNO supply constraints.

universal_questions.question: What age bracket is the property?
universal_questions.rationale: Pre-1970s properties may have legacy wiring, no RCD and no earth.

universal_questions.question: Which floor is the work on?
universal_questions.rationale: Upper floors mean longer cable runs and loft access considerations.

universal_questions.question: Where is the consumer unit (fuse board) located?
universal_questions.rationale: Distance from the consumer unit affects cable run length and labour time.

universal_questions.question: How old is the consumer unit?
universal_questions.rationale: Pre-2000 boards often lack modern protection and may need upgrading.

universal_questions.question: Are you the owner, tenant or landlord?
universal_questions.rationale: Landlords have 5-year EICR obligations; tenants need landlord permission.

universal_questions.question: Is there parking available near the property?
universal_questions.rationale: Parking constraints affect travel time and cost, especially in London.

universal_questions.question: When would you like the work done?
universal_questions.rationale: Urgency and weekend work carry premium pricing.

universal_questions.question: Can you upload a photo of the area or existing fitting?
universal_questions.rationale: Photos help assess access, wall type and existing wiring condition.

universal_questions.question: Do you know what type of earthing system the property has?
universal_questions.rationale: Determines bonding conductor size, RCD requirements and whether PME earth can be exported to outbuildings.

universal_questions.question: Is your electrician registered with a Competent Person Scheme?
universal_questions.rationale: CPS registration determines whether notifiable work can be self-certified or must go through building control.

job_categories.name: Power Distribution
job_categories.description: Consumer units, rewires and distribution to outbuildings.

specific_questions.question: What type of board do you currently have?
specific_questions.rationale: Older boards usually need full replacement.

specific_questions.question: How many circuits does the property have (or bedrooms if unsure)?
specific_questions.rationale: Determines the size of board required.

specific_questions.question: Would you like surge protection (SPD) included?
specific_questions.rationale: SPDs protect against transient overvoltage and are recommended since Amendment 3.

specific_questions.question: Would you like arc-fault detection (AFDD) included?
specific_questions.rationale: AFDDs detect dangerous arc faults and are increasingly recommended.

specific_questions.question: Are you planning any future additions (EV charger, extension, solar, hot tub)?
specific_questions.rationale: Future-proofing affects spare-way requirements.

specific_questions.question: How many bedrooms does the property have?
specific_questions.rationale: Drives circuit count and material quantities.

specific_questions.question: Is the property occupied during the rewire?
specific_questions.rationale: Occupied properties take longer due to access constraints.

specific_questions.question: What floor and wall construction is typical?
specific_questions.rationale: Solid construction increases chasing and making-good costs.

specific_questions.question: Do you want the rewire to include networking / data cabling?
specific_questions.rationale: Adds low-voltage cabling and outlets.

specific_questions.question: Which parts of the property need rewiring?
specific_questions.rationale: Defines scope and circuit count.

specific_questions.question: Is the existing consumer unit modern with spare ways?
specific_questions.rationale: May require a CU upgrade as part of the work.

specific_questions.question: What will the outbuilding be used for?
specific_questions.rationale: Determines load and whether a sub-CU is needed.

specific_questions.question: How far is the outbuilding from the house?
specific_questions.rationale: Distance drives cable size and voltage drop.

specific_questions.question: Will the cable run underground?
specific_questions.rationale: Underground runs need SWA cable and often deeper burial.

job_categories.name: Lighting
job_categories.description: Indoor and outdoor lighting installations and upgrades.

specific_questions.question: Is this a like-for-like replacement or a new location?
specific_questions.rationale: New locations may require new cable runs.

specific_questions.question: What type of fitting is being installed?
specific_questions.rationale: Weight and mounting method affect labour.

specific_questions.question: What room is the fitting in?
specific_questions.rationale: Bathroom and outdoor fittings have IP rating requirements.

job_types.name: Additional Downlights
job_types.part_p_notifiable: Conditional — yes if new circuits / special locations

specific_questions.question: How many downlights do you want?
specific_questions.rationale: Drives material and labour quantities.

specific_questions.question: Are the ceilings fire-rated (e.g. separating floors)?
specific_questions.rationale: Fire-rated downlights are required for fire-rated ceilings.

specific_questions.question: Do you want them dimmable?
specific_questions.rationale: Requires dimmable lamps and compatible dimmer switches.

specific_questions.question: What type of ceiling do you have?
specific_questions.rationale: Affects cutting and fixing difficulty.

specific_questions.question: How many outdoor lights are required?
specific_questions.rationale: Drives cable and labour estimates.

specific_questions.question: Will they be switched from inside?
specific_questions.rationale: Affects switching cable runs.

specific_questions.question: Do you want PIR / motion sensors?
specific_questions.rationale: Adds sensor cost and commissioning time.

specific_questions.question: Which bathroom zone will the fitting go in?
specific_questions.rationale: Determines permitted equipment and IP rating.

specific_questions.question: What type of fitting?
specific_questions.rationale: Different fittings have different zone and RCD requirements.

job_categories.name: Power Points
job_categories.description: Sockets, USB outlets, outdoor sockets and fused connection units.

job_types.name: Additional Socket Outlet
job_types.part_p_notifiable: Conditional — kitchen/bathroom/new circuit = Yes; elsewhere spur = No

specific_questions.question: What type of socket do you want?
specific_questions.rationale: USB/smart sockets cost more but add functionality.

specific_questions.question: Which room will the socket be in?
specific_questions.rationale: Kitchen and bathroom sockets are notifiable and often need dedicated circuits.

specific_questions.question: What will you be plugging into this socket?
specific_questions.rationale: High-power appliances need dedicated circuits.

specific_questions.question: Is there an existing socket nearby on the same wall?
specific_questions.rationale: Determines whether a spur or new circuit is needed.

specific_questions.question: How far is the nearest socket from the consumer unit?
specific_questions.rationale: Longer runs increase cable size and labour.

specific_questions.question: Do you need USB-A, USB-C or both?
specific_questions.rationale: Affects accessory cost and future-proofing.

specific_questions.question: Do you want smart-home integration?
specific_questions.rationale: Determines compatibility requirements.

specific_questions.question: How many outdoor sockets do you want?
specific_questions.rationale: Drives cable and accessory count.

specific_questions.question: What will they be used for?
specific_questions.rationale: High-power uses may need dedicated circuits.

specific_questions.question: Is the cable run likely to be over 20m?
specific_questions.rationale: Longer runs may need thicker SWA cable.

specific_questions.question: What appliance will the FCU supply?
specific_questions.rationale: Determines load and cable size.

specific_questions.question: Will the appliance be on a new circuit or spur from an existing?
specific_questions.rationale: New circuits are notifiable.

job_categories.name: Heating & Cooking
job_categories.description: High-demand fixed appliances requiring dedicated circuits.

specific_questions.question: What kW rating is the shower?
specific_questions.rationale: kW rating determines cable size, breaker and supply requirements.

specific_questions.question: How far is the shower from the consumer unit?
specific_questions.rationale: Distance affects cable sizing and voltage drop.

specific_questions.question: Is your water system gravity-fed or mains-pressure?
specific_questions.rationale: Low pressure may need a pumped shower or lower kW rating.

specific_questions.question: Is this a like-for-like replacement or a new install/upgrade?
specific_questions.rationale: Upgrades may need larger cable and breaker.

specific_questions.question: What type of cooking appliance?
specific_questions.rationale: Load varies from 13A to 45A+.

specific_questions.question: What is the rated power (kW) if known?
specific_questions.rationale: Used to size cable and breaker.

specific_questions.question: Is there an existing cooker circuit?
specific_questions.rationale: Existing circuit may be reusable if sized correctly.

specific_questions.question: How many storage heaters need connecting?
specific_questions.rationale: Drives circuit and control wiring requirements.

specific_questions.question: Are the heaters over 30 years old?
specific_questions.rationale: Old heaters may contain asbestos — specialist removal needed.

specific_questions.question: Do you have an off-peak / Economy 7 supply?
specific_questions.rationale: Controls and wiring differ for off-peak tariffs.

job_categories.name: Specialist
job_categories.description: EV chargers, alarms, inspections and security.

specific_questions.question: Do you have off-street parking?
specific_questions.rationale: On-street parking often makes installation impractical.

specific_questions.question: What kW charger do you want?
specific_questions.rationale: 7kW is standard for single-phase UK homes; 22kW needs three-phase.

specific_questions.question: How far will the charger be from the consumer unit?
specific_questions.rationale: Distance drives cable size and labour.

specific_questions.question: Do you have an electric shower, heat pump, or other large loads?
specific_questions.rationale: May trigger supply capacity check with DNO.

specific_questions.question: Is there Wi-Fi coverage at the charger location?
specific_questions.rationale: Smart chargers require an internet connection.

specific_questions.question: Do you want tethered or untethered?
specific_questions.rationale: Affects unit cost and convenience.

specific_questions.question: How many alarms are needed?
specific_questions.rationale: Drives material and labour count.

specific_questions.question: Do they need to be interlinked?
specific_questions.rationale: Scottish law and new builds require interlinking.

specific_questions.question: What rooms need coverage?
specific_questions.rationale: Determines smoke vs heat detector mix.

specific_questions.question: Why do you need the EICR?
specific_questions.rationale: Affects urgency and reporting detail.

specific_questions.question: How many circuits does the property have?
specific_questions.rationale: Drives inspection time and cost.

specific_questions.question: Is the property occupied?
specific_questions.rationale: Access arrangements differ.

specific_questions.question: What type of security system?
specific_questions.rationale: Determines power and data requirements.

specific_questions.question: How many devices need wiring?
specific_questions.rationale: Drives cable and labour estimates.

notifiability_rules.customer_impact: Registered electrician required; EIC certificate issued.
Registered electrician required; Building Control notified.

notifiability_rules.condition: additional socket via ring spur in non-kitchen/bathroom
notifiability_rules.customer_impact: Any competent person; no certificate required.
Registered electrician mandatory; BS 7671 Section 701 applies.

notifiability_rules.condition: electrical work in kitchen (new circuit/additional sockets)

notifiability_rules.customer_impact: Registered electrician; IP and RCD requirements apply.
OZEV-approved installer; DNO notification may be required.
Registered electrician; interlinking required in Scotland.

pricing_adjustment_factors.factor: Solid concrete floors or dot-and-dab walls

compliance_flags.response: Suggest a consumer unit upgrade for RCD protection.

compliance_flags.trigger: Property > 50 years with no recent EICR
Bathroom work with no RCD confirmed
compliance_flags.response: All bathroom circuits MUST have 30mA RCD protection.
This appliance needs a dedicated circuit, not a spur.

compliance_flags.trigger: Outdoor work with no RCD confirmed
compliance_flags.response: Outdoor circuits MUST have RCD protection.

compliance_flags.trigger: EV charger with supply <100A or other large loads
compliance_flags.response: A supply capacity check may be needed; the DNO may need notification.
May contain asbestos — specialist removal may be required.

compliance_flags.trigger: Scotland property with alarms not interlinked
Socket circuit ≤32A, bathroom circuit, outdoor circuit or EV circuit
compliance_flags.response: Minimum Type A 30mA RCD protection is required. Type AC is no longer adequate for most modern loads.

compliance_flags.trigger: HRRB, HMO, care home, student accommodation or occupant unable to maintain installation
compliance_flags.response: AFDDs are mandatory on socket circuits ≤32A. Owner-occupied dwellings should be offered AFDDs as a recommendation.

compliance_flags.trigger: EV charger installed outdoors or in an accessible location on a PME supply
compliance_flags.response: A PME earthing risk assessment is required. A TT earth rod or PEN fault detection device may be needed.
All circuits require 30mA RCD protection; an earth electrode must be verified; a Type 2 SPD is typically required.

compliance_flags.trigger: Notifiable work and electrician is not CPS registered
compliance_flags.response: The homeowner must notify building control and pay a fee (typically £200-£400). Itemise this or state it is the customer's responsibility.

compliance_flags.trigger: EICR records C1, C2 or FI observations
compliance_flags.response: Remedial work is required. C1 danger present must be made safe; C2 urgent remedial within 28 days. Quote remedial work separately.

conversational_guidelines.persona: Friendly, patient, non-technical electrical expert. Never uses jargon without explanation. Always offers 'I don't know' as a valid answer. Uses progressive disclosure. Validates intent before technical detail.

phases.name: Intent & Essentials
phases.goal: Confirm what the customer wants, where, and flag immediate red flags.

phases.name: Site Assessment
phases.goal: Gather information an electrician would assess on survey; note unknowns for on-site verification.

phases.name: Detail & Confirmation
phases.goal: Final technical details, photo upload request, and summary preview.

handling_idk.default_and_note: No problem — most people don't know. I'll note it as 'to be confirmed on site'.
handling_idk.infer_from_context: Use property age / type to make an educated guess, presented for electrician confirmation.
handling_idk.use_photos: Request a photo after 3-5 questions when the customer is engaged.

conversational_guidelines.photo_guidance: Request photos only after engagement. Explain why the photo helps (e.g. fuse board type, wall construction, access). Never request a photo as the first question.
design_principles: Customers don't know what electricians need to know.
Notifiability is the most important compliance flag.
Property age is the strongest price predictor.
Distance from the consumer unit determines cable cost.
Regional pricing varies by up to 2x across the UK.
Photos are requested after engagement, not at the start.
Bundle recommendations increase average order value.
Set expectations about exclusions (making good, decorating, flooring).
The conversation should feel like advice, not a form.
